title: Cards Show Their Tags
eyebrow: Live on your board, and now ticked off as well

actions.fyi: Both things that held the tick up are fixed — the cross-repository check, and the rule that refused a finished piece its tick. This job is ticking off now and nothing on this page is waiting on you.

content.label: What the card shows now
content.lead: Every card names the system it belongs to and the kind of work it is, in colour.

before.caption: Before: a card said Task and nothing else

after.caption: After: the system, and the kind of work

blocks.text: The word Task is gone from the corner. It was on 385 cards and Epic on 165, and neither ever told you whether the card was a fault, new work or upkeep — that lives in the tags.

content.label: Reading the board by one system, or one kind
content.lead: A tag picker sits beside the type picker; the board narrows to what you chose.

shots.caption: Pick a system or a kind; each carries the colour it wears on the cards
Narrowed to new work: 11 cards, and every one of them is new work

blocks.text: Picking two systems widens the board to both; picking a system and a kind narrows it to cards that are both. It stacks with the search box.

content.label: Checked, not eyeballed
content.lead: A check reads the tags off the running screen and argues with the work list.

rows: Cards whose tags reach the screen
Cards drawn under a tag that lack it
Cards carrying a tag that the filter hid
Rules held by a test that goes red
Re-checked today, on a board grown to 182 cards

blocks.text: The nine cards with no tags at all really have none: they are made by a side path that skips the tagging, which is now its own card.
All fifteen rules are green today, and weakening the filter on purpose makes the right one go red while the others stay green — so they are watching something.

content.label: The colours
content.lead: The same card reads on a dark board and a light one, without a second palette.

blocks.text: Each tag carries a colour of its own and everything else about it is mixed against whichever board you are on, so it lands readable either way with nothing to keep in step.

decisions.title: Only two tags are drawn: the system, and the kind of work
decisions.why: A card also carries bookkeeping tags that mean nothing to you. Drawing them would bury the two that do.

decisions.title: The kind of work takes the corner where Task used to sit
decisions.why: Task or Epic is the card's shape, never its kind, and the two never once agreed across 551 cards. One corner, one meaning.

decisions.title: A fault is red, new work blue, upkeep amber; a system keeps one colour forever
decisions.why: The three kinds are fixed so they read at a glance. Systems are open-ended, so each takes a colour from its own name — no list to keep, and it never shifts.

decisions.title: One picker, two sections, many picks
decisions.why: Two pickers would double the row for something you use one at a time. Picks inside a section widen, across sections they narrow.

decisions.title: A card with no tags keeps the old badge
decisions.why: Nine cards have none. Showing an empty space would read as a fault in the screen rather than in the card.

decisions.title: The check drives the real screen, not a copy of it
decisions.why: It opens your board in a browser, reads what was drawn, works the picker and compares both directions against the work list. It cannot come back green while the screen is wrong.

next.if_nothing: The tags stay live on your board and the job finishes ticking itself off. Nothing here is waiting on you.
